subject: Order form redlines: VPC deployment - evidence split & operator access
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@healthspectrum.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: legal@healthspectrum.com, dpo@healthspectrum.com
Date: 2027-11-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthSpectrum - Order Form redlines for VPC deployment

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement and security teams reviewed the Order Form and MSA exhibits and returned a handful of redlines focused on the private VPC/on-prem deployment path. High-level asks below (attached: HealthSpectrum_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf):

- License perimeter: clarify whether runtime snapshots used for forensic review are covered by the customer license or a provider copy; we need clarity on permitted use for retained artifacts.
- Operator access: proposal for ephemeral operator access windows (witnessing vs. limited console access) and an auditable handover record.
- Evidence/escrow: because of our regulatory profile, we asked for an escrow-like mechanism or notarized snapshot hashes for forensic purposes — they prefer a process that doesn't require full software escrow but provides verifiable proof of continuity.
- Audit window & SLAs: short conflict about temporary audit console access during a scheduled window and liability carveouts.

Can Redwood propose a concise exhibit / playbook we can attach to the Order Form that addresses these points? We need language we can show Security and our procurement team this week. If easier, happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Attachments: HealthSpectrum_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf (PDF)

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
Head of IT Procurement
HealthSpectrum
[Attachment: HealthSpectrum_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf (application/pdf)]

Rajiv — thanks for the clear note and the attached redlines. We can absolutely provide a targeted exhibit and a short playbook that maps the legal language to operational controls (operator access model, snapshot/verification flow, and an audit window process).

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
1) I'll loop in Legal (Laura) and Infra (David) to draft the exhibit and a runbook.
2) We'll propose two options: (A) witness-lite approach with notarized snapshot hashes + signed affidavit, or (B) time-boxed operator witness with scoped console session and recorded logs (preferred for higher-assurance customers).
3) We'll send redline-friendly language and a one-page runbook by EOD tomorrow. If that looks good, we can provide a DocuSign-ready snippet for the Order Form.

Propose 11/09 11:00am PT for a quick 30-min alignment with you + security if needed — here's a calendar link: https://calendar.example/vanessa/30min/HS-4391-review

Best,

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-07T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealthSpectrum - Order Form redlines for VPC deployment (internal)

Folks — forwarding Rajiv's redlines (below). We need a tight deliverable to get this over the line: legal snippets for the Order Form + a short operational playbook (1-2 pages) that maps to the snippets. Points we must address:

- License perimeter: propose explicit line: "Customer retains ownership of data and any Customer-originated snapshots; Redwood retains a transient provider runtime copy solely for the purpose of support and forensic review for the duration of the audit window; any retained artifacts beyond the audit window require express exhibit approval."
- Snapshot verification: recommend using SHA-256 hashes produced at snapshot creation and recorded in a signed affidavit to avoid full code escrow.
- Operator access: recommend ephemeral access via time-limited IAM session + mandatory session recording + KMS-wrapped decryption keys; provide option for witnessless notarized hash if customer prohibits console access.
- Audit window: limit to scheduled 8-hour window per request, with a 48-hour notice period; include SLA exceptions and indemnity carveout language.

Deliverables:
- Laura: legal-ready Order Form Exhibit language (snippets and alternatives) — target EOD tomorrow.
- David: runbook draft + list of artifacts we can produce and how they're hashed/recorded — target EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — we need to keep the language minimal and procurement-friendly.

—Vanessa

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-07T11:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthSpectrum - Order Form redlines for VPC deployment (internal)

Vanessa / Laura — quick technical read and what we can commit to:

- Snapshots: we can produce encrypted runtime snapshots and publish a SHA-256 hash at creation time. The snapshot file itself will be stored in an internal S3 bucket for a configurable retention (default 7 days). We can include a signed manifest (signed by Redwood infra key) referencing the snapshot hash.
- Notarized hash: Redwood Legal can sign an affidavit referencing the manifest; if customer prefers a third-party notarization, we can export the manifest for client-side notarization (customer handles notarization logistics).
- Operator access: we support time-limited bastion sessions with session recording (stored for 30 days) and KMS envelope-wrapped credentials. We can restrict commands and provide a pre-approved runbook for witness sessions.
- Evidence artifacts we can deliver: manifest (json line), snapshot hash, session recording (mp4), access logs (syslog export), KMS audit records.

Attachment: Redwood_PrivateDeploy_Runbook_Draft.md (stubbed runbook) — will refine once Laura confirms legal constraints.

Technical caveats:
- We cannot provide live R/W access to production state outside of controlled sessions; any snapshot access for customer forensic review requires a secure transfer mechanism (SFTP OR signed temporary token).
- For high-assurance notarization we recommend the witness path (operator session) or third-party notarization; both are feasible but require procurement lead time.

—David
Director, Infrastructure & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PrivateDeploy_Runbook_Draft.md (text)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@healthspectrum.com>, legal@healthspectrum.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-07T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSpectrum - Order Form redlines for VPC deployment

Rajiv — thanks for the redlines. Please find below proposed short-form Order Form Exhibit language (two options) and a one-page explanation of the operational controls. If either option is acceptable we will prepare a DocuSign exhibit (link below) and provide the runbook reference.

Option 1 (witness-lite; preferred):
"Exhibit X — Evidence and Operator Access. Redwood will, upon Customer request and subject to the terms below, produce verifiable artifacts to support Customer audits: (i) an encrypted runtime snapshot and an associated SHA-256 hash; (ii) a signed manifest attesting to snapshot creation; and (iii) session recordings and access logs for any operator sessions. Customer may elect either: (A) a notarized-hash path in which Redwood provides the signed manifest and snapshot hash for Customer-orchestrated notarization, or (B) a time-limited operator witness session performed by Redwood under a documented runbook. Operator sessions are subject to a 48-hour notice period and will be recorded and retained for thirty (30) days."
Option 2 (minimal/no-console):
"Exhibit X — Evidence-only path. Redwood will provide encrypted snapshot artifacts and signed manifest (SHA-256) for Customer notarization. No operator console sessions will be made available. Redwood's retention of provider copies will not exceed seven (7) days absent express Exhibit approval."
Operational summary (one page):
- Snapshot creation: Redwood infra creates encrypted snapshot, computes SHA-256, publishes signed manifest.
- Transfer: secure SFTP or pre-signed time-limited object URL.
- Operator session: limited to pre-approved runbook; recording, KMS-wrapped keys, and access logs delivered post-session.
- Audit window: one 8-hour window per request with 48-hour notice.

If HealthSpectrum prefers Option 1, we'll issue a DocuSign-ready snippet and include an explicit exhibit to the Order Form. DocuSign draft (preview): https://docusign.example/HS-4391-orderform

Next steps: please tell us which option you prefer and whether Security wants any additional controls (e.g., independent notarization vendor). If you want to talk through today, I'm available 4:00–5:00pm PT.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_ExhibitA_snippet.pdf (pdf)]
